name: mycrew
description: A four-layer harness for Claude Code, each layer driving the one below: primitives and house rules, a pipeline that carries a task from decision to hardened code, a product plane holding what the product must do, and a chief on top that shapes the plane and dispatches its workers. Beside the layers, characters you start a session as. Install mycrew-tools first.

plugins.name: mycrew-tools
plugins.description: Layer 1/4 — the primitives. Small, project-agnostic skills you reach for mid-work: /slap resets a fix that has stopped working, /likec4 draws architecture as code, /reminder pins a rule as a hard constraint, /retract hunts down information declared wrong and cuts it out. Ships the house rule files too. Everything above builds on this.

plugins.name: mycrew-pipeline
plugins.description: Layer 2/4 — the build pipeline. Six stages carry one task from a decision to shipped code: /how-to-do settles the fork, /do builds it, then /refactor, /review, /secure and /test harden it. In review and secure, the eyes that hunt are never the author's. Every stage weighs what actually changed and skips in one honest line when the change doesn't earn it.

plugins.name: mycrew-product
plugins.description: Layer 3/4 — the product plane: everything true about the whole product, above the sub-projects. /product-init founds it. /braindump and /ask-me draw the product out of you and file each piece where it belongs; /propose-idea is the one that puts an idea in, and only on your approval. Whatever you affirm, wherever you affirm it, product-rules is the one rule set that decides where it lands and in what shape. /propose-design and /propose-architecture settle how the product looks and how it is built — argued out against every alternative they beat, then handed straight to work and never written down, because the built UI and the running code are the only truth about either.

plugins.name: mycrew-chief
plugins.description: Layer 4/4 — your deputy over the whole product. /chief reads the plane, breaks an approved feature into per-repo assignments, sequences them provider-first, dispatches the worker it ships as subagents, and takes or sends back what comes home. It never decides what the product should do, and never writes code. It conducts; the workers build.

plugins.name: mycrew-agents
plugins.description: Not a layer — who you are talking to. Characters you start a session as: name one when you dispatch the session (`@mentor …`) and it runs as that character, with its own stance and its own limits. One so far — mentor, the one you think a question through with, who never solves it for you.
